newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Austere Dutch to ditch long Euro lunches.
newsitem.headline: Austere Dutch to ditch long Euro lunches.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers will be subject to tighter-than-usual dietary discipline during ministerial councils under the Dutch EU presidency, Dutch media reported on Friday.

Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo has long disliked the two-and-a-half hour working lunches at which ministers discuss the Union's external relations and has decided as current chairman to do away with them, the Dutch news agency ANP said.

At next Monday's General Council meeting in Brussels the foreign ministers will negotiate over EU foreign policy before they go in to lunch, which will last only around an hour, a Dutch Foreign Ministry spokeswoman confirmed.
"It is a slightly different way of approaching the decision-making process," she said.

The Dutch daily de Volkskrant quoted diplomatic sources as saying past lunches had often been chaotic, with various discussions under way around the table and ministers often leaving with different impressions of what was concluded.
After attending his first ministerial council, Van Mierlo had expressed amazement that matters like the war in the former Yugoslavia could be discussed between bites of salmon, ANP said.
